correctness.rationale: Exact autonomous binomial particle-count projection and finite-state uniqueness prove the weak-exchange mixture. Strict Newton inequalities on normalized symmetric means establish every local MTP2 cross-product ratio; FKG and MTP2 closure give global positive association and strictly positive all-pair covariances. Unnormalized elementary-symmetric inequalities give negative canonical pair covariance; horizontal balance and vertical telescoping give the driven multi-lane example. The 64-state checker and 240 randomized cases corroborate and do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The mixture and its multi-dimensional sector weights are known from arXiv:2405.09261v1, arXiv:2403.01934v1, and precursor arXiv:1711.06949. The strict MTP2 and pair-sign reversal, all-site equality boundary and finite-rate implication are not stated in these inspected works. Classical Newton and FKG are credited; exact aliases and implication comparisons found no covering prior mathematical record. Residual uncertainty persists for unindexed biased-sampling and correlation-literature results.
residual_risks: Literature search does not certify priority; a known combinatorial theorem for binomial mixtures of Fisher weighted fixed-size subsets might imply the full MTP2 property.
General FKG reference inspected at theorem level, not entire publisher article; reliance is on standard inequality, not claimed novelty.
Finite-rate strict positivity is only locally uniform in epsilon for each fixed finite network, not uniformly in site count.

value.rationale: Resolves a natural all-distance sign reversal in driven, hardcore-repulsive exclusion systems: strict negative co-occupation in each fixed-number sector but strict positive co-occupation under the physically motivated rare Langmuir exchange. Full increasing-event association, exact homogeneous equality and a finite-positive-reaction persistence theorem distinguish the claim from a routine isolated finite-size calculation; nonzero transverse circulation preserves physical interest.
